visualReview.selection: Every production comparison below0.48 on a gained page plus its actual template staff, and p2/staff9,p8/staff9,p16/staff7 boundary regressions.
visualReview.reviewMethod: All13 freshly rendered contact sheets individually viewed; sampled patch polygons reconstructed from native event coordinates over original PDF images. Also viewed original-source p2/staff9 production-v3 comparison.
findings: Every gained source page visibly contains one complete22-staff system:11orchestral wind/brass/timpani staves,6vocal staves with divided alto and bass sections,5string staves. No subgroup treated as whole system.
All61 selected new patch locations cover the intended printed G/F clef at the source left boundary. No patch starts on interior notes or an isolated exterior bracket in these reviewed cases.
Some patches retain instrument-label letters/key signatures and brace tails. This is layout/clef resemblance with reviewed seed identities, not semantic instrument recognition.
p2/staff9 now samples the printed F clef rather than the later interior-note/barline region. p8/staff9 keeps bracket and true system boundary distinct; p16/staff7 accepts the thick genuine boundary.

preservedContracts: All grouping/connection/outside-boundary checks remain before anchoring.
Only patch and boundaryPatchProven fields change on the returned StaffFeature; original lines/start/end continue to define source bounds. Localphase only affects temporary patch sampling.
Exactly one distinct source-supported band required. Only overlapping bands merge; disjoint boundaries are not averaged.
Matching requires equal per-staff origin provenance; a proven patch is never compared with an unproven original patch. Both-original behavior is preserved.
Unchanged clef confidence thresholds0.48/0.72; no new barCount/startBarNumber inference.
Existing explicit reviewed assignment and user acceptance remain required.
limits: Cancellation runtime below one whole score was not measured in this review; root is testing the clean integration separately.
